outputs.final_proof:
\begin{proof}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be any collection of subspaces of $V$, and define
\[
S=\bigcap_{U\in\mathcal{C}}U.
\]
The set $S$ is contained in $V$. If $\mathcal{C}=\varnothing$, its intersection is conventionally $V$, which is a subspace. Suppose now that $\mathcal{C}$ is nonempty. Every $U\in\mathcal{C}$ contains $0$, so $0\in S$. If $x,y\in S$, then $x,y$ belong to every $U\in\mathcal{C}$. Since each such $U$ is closed under addition, $x+y$ belongs to every $U\in\mathcal{C}$, hence $x+y\in S$. If $a\in F$ and $x\in S$, then $x\in U$ for every $U\in\mathcal{C}$, and scalar closure gives $ax\in U$ for every $U\in\mathcal{C}$. Thus $ax\in S$. Therefore $S$ is a subspace of $V$.
\end{proof}
